definition: Skill chaining is a skill discovery method in continuous reinforcement learning.
details: It has been extended to high-dimensional continuous domains by the related Deep skill chaining algorithm.

explainer.lead: Skill chaining is a skill discovery method in continuous reinforcement learning. It matters because it lets agents build up complex behaviour by learning and linking reusable skills, and the related Deep skill chaining algorithm extends it to high-dimensional continuous domains.

tiers.eli5: Instead of learning one giant task all at once, the agent learns small tricks one by one and chains them together, like learning to walk before learning to run.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use skill chaining to discover reusable skills in continuous control settings, with Deep skill chaining handling high-dimensional domains. A pitfall is that chained skills must connect reliably, so how skills are linked matters as much as how each one is learned.
tiers.paperLevel: A skill discovery method for continuous reinforcement learning, extended to high-dimensional continuous domains by the related Deep skill chaining algorithm; its scope is skill discovery rather than a general-purpose learning recipe.

explainer.example: An agent in a continuous control task first learns a simple skill, then chains further skills onto it to accomplish a longer-horizon task.
